texts: Now let us look closely at the two most important scenarios. A fight, and a weapon.
A fight. The model detects sharp movement between two or more people, from their posture and the speed of motion.
The frame and the incident video are stored automatically. A high level alert appears on the panel and an audible signal on the control screen.
The security officer gets a notification and the camera point on the map. If the student is recognised, the parent is notified too.

The incident enters the log automatically and is attached to that person's history. Statistics then show where and when fights repeat. If the pattern continues, a referral to the prevention inspector is generated.
The weapon scenario is different. Here the system does not wait for confirmation.
As soon as the model finds a weapon-like object, the level becomes critical at once. A siren, a full screen alarm on every control screen, and the camera stream opens automatically.

Management and the responsible officer are notified at the same moment. A ready case file — frame, video, time and place — is sent automatically to the National Guard and the Ministry of Internal Affairs.
If the signal was wrong, the responsible officer flags it and the model threshold is tuned automatically for that specific camera.
